name: Neon Terminal
tagline: Typed commands, green phosphor glow, a glitch cut to the logo.
description: Green-phosphor terminal look: black screen, glowing mono type that types itself with a block cursor, line-by-line readouts with check marks, scanlines over everything and glitch cuts. The preview is a developer-tool launch that types a real command and ends on an install chip.

rhythm.notes: Output lines every 0.3–0.4s, like a real CLI. Hold the final URL line ~1s before the glitch.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Black #050806 screen with green phosphor: primary #3dff8f with a soft glow (text-shadow), muted #4f7a5d for secondary text, yellow ▲ for highlights. A scanline overlay (repeating 2px lines, 22% black) stays above everything.
- Everything is monospace (JetBrains Mono-like): the subject is told through typed lines, ASCII or line-drawn diagrams in green strokes, progress readouts, counters and status lists with check marks.
- Type text with a width tween and steps(<characters>), ~22 chars per second, with a blinking block cursor (0.01s opacity yoyo, 0.25s repeatDelay). Output lines reveal one by one.
- Content should feel real and specific: believable numbers, timings, names and labels, never lorem ipsum.
- Transition out with 3–4 quick skewX jitters (0.05s) then fade; reveal a title by squeezing scaleX from 1.6 to 1 with expo.out (animate transforms, not letter-spacing).
- Optional motif: a terminal window with a title bar, and a pill-shaped command chip in the primary green.
- Avoid other colours, photos, rounded friendly UI and smooth decorative motion.
example: The preview is a developer-tool launch: a terminal types a real command, output lines pop in with check marks, then a glitch reveals the product name and an install chip. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
